Each seat binds to one routable address block. At join the applicant publishes a signed TXT record under a domain it controls; the node resolves it under DNSSEC, opens a TCP inlet on port 443 and waits for a pulse derived from the epoch challenge. A wrong signal closes the seat. The block must be announced by an AS the registry ties to the applicant, and fifty clones inside one /24 count once.

A /24 trades near 12,000 dollars plus a 550 dollar AS fee, so fifty seats cost about 600,000 dollars before any bandwidth.

A doorbell rings loud or soft, yet the chime stays in one house.
